 JUDGMENT

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 09.11.2017.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, SCCH - 25 3 MVC No. 6361/2018 On 09.11.2017 at about 11.40am the petitioner and his wife were going on their Active Honda two wheeler bearing No.KA-04-HX-4788 towards Doddanakundi.

At that time the respondent No.1/Driver of the Car bearing No.KA-01-MM- 4326 drove the car in high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed the petitioner's Two wheeler from the hind side and caused the accident.

Due to impact both fell down and the petitioner suffered grievous injuries resulted in undergoing surgery and spent about Rs.7,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food and nourishment etc.,

At the time of accident the petitioner was working as a Supervisor at ADD On Kitchens and earning Rs.50,000/-
per month.
Due to accidental injuries he lost his employment and lost his income.
He is put to great hardship and mental agony and shock.
The accident caused due to the carelessness, rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA- 01-MM-4326.
The KR Puram Traffic Police have registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.0410/2017 p/u/Sec.279, 337, 338 of IPC.

Therefore, SCCH - 25 4 MVC No. 6361/2018 the 1st respondent being the driver, 2nd respondent being the RC Owner and the 3rd respondent being the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him.
Hence, this petition.
3. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondent Nos.2 & 3 appeared through their respective counsel and filed separate written statements.
In spite of due service of summons the respondent No.1 did not appear hence placed exparte.
4. The objection of the respondent No.2.
She has denied the petition averments.

She has denied the manner of accident, medical expenses,
petitioner's job and income.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant, excessive, imaginary and without any basis.
5. The objection of the respondent No.3.

sentences.text: It has denied all the averments of the petition except admitting the issuance of the policy in favour of the Respondent No.2 in respect of the Car vehicle bearing KA-01- MM-4326.
The driver of the Car did not have valid and effective DL and also FC to ply the vehicle as on the date of accident.
The accident caused due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.
He has denied the manner of accident.
Further the petition is not maintainable for nonjoinder of the owner and the insurer of the motorcycle.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
The petitioners have in collusion with the police changed the driver in the records.
It has also denied the age, occupation and the manner of accident.
It contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive, arbitrary and disproportionate.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
SCCH - 25 6 MVC No. 6361/2018 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-1-MM-4326 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or award?
7. The Petitioner in order to prove his case has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.20 and Exs.22 to 24.
Dr.Chethan Nagaraj got examined as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.21.

On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.
8.
Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.

On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3: As per the final order,
 for the following:-
 REASONS  10. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MM-4326, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 by Ravi Shankar .K.B vs Naveen .N on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136487906/
3 reiterating the petition averments in his chief examination affidavit and produced 8 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.8.

sentences.text: During his cross-examination he has admitted that the offending vehicle was Car bearing No.KA-01-MM- 4326.
The complaint was registered by his wife even though the police had come to the hospital on the same day.
The Two wheeler belonged to his wife.
The accident spot is a junction and does not have a signal.
11. The accident occurred on 09.11.2017 and the FIR SCCH - 25 8 MVC No. 6361/2018 was registered on the same day on the complaint of petitioner's wife.
The Mahazar at Ex.P.2 was conducted on 10.11.2017 at about 09.00am to 10.00am.
The Sketch at Ex.P.3 shows that the accident occurred in the middle of the Road.
After thorough investigation, the investigation officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending Car at Ex.P.4.
Ex . P.5
statement of witness gives the details of the accident through witness.
The Ex.P.6 Notice u/Sec.133 of MV Act sent to the RC owner about full details of the accident and also reply to that notice.
Wound Certificate at Ex.P.7 shows that the petitioner has suffered injuries in an RTA on 09.11.2017 at about 30.30pm.
Ex.P.8 MVA report shows that the vehicle bearing No.KA-04-HX-4788 damaged to its rear left side body.
The Respondent No.3 has contended that the accident occurred due to 50% contributory negligence of the petitioner and the sole negligence of the rider of the Honda Activa.
But in order to prove the same they have neither produced any documents nor examined any witness.

Therefore, on the basis of the evidence of PW.1 and the SCCH - 25 9 MVC No. 6361/2018 documents before the court Exs.P.1 to P.8, the Tribunal holds that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-01-MM-4326.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate at Ex.P.7.
As per Ex.P.7 the petitioner has suffered (i) Fracture both bone right leg and (ii) Suspected fracture of injuries Pubic Rami which are grievous in nature.
13. The petitioner has got examined Dr.Chethan Nagaraj as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.21 Case sheet.
He has deposed the details of surgery undergone by the petitioner and diagnosed (a) closed comminuted fracture of right tibia shaft and (b) closed fracture right proximal tibia.
He further stated that the petitioner is suffering from physical aspects and functional impairment of 25% of right lower limb and around 12% of the whole body.
PW.2 in his cross examination has stated that he has treated the petitioner once in 2017 & once in 2018.
Further admitted that the treatment given in 2018 are not related to the accident.
But it was weakness in the right leg which was due to the injuries suffered in 2017.
Further sated that the only one fracture was operated and other fracture is treated conservatively.
One of the fractures is deformed and other one is united.

Further suggested that the petitioner can perform co-ordinated Ravi Shankar .K.B vs Naveen .N on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136487906/
4 activities with some difficulties.

Disability:
15.
From the evidence of PW.2 and the documents on record, it is clear that the petitioner has suffered closed comminuted fracture of right tibia shaft and closed fracture right proximal tibia.
He has averred that the petitioner was working as a Supervisor at ADD On Kitchen.
He has stated that he can work with some difficulties.
This means that either he has to sit or stand for a long time.
This kind of disability SCCH - 25 11 MVC No. 6361/2018 will affect his day to day work.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the functional disability at 10%.

Monthly income:
16.
The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was working as Supervisor at ADD on Kitchen and earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
In this regard he has produced Ex.P.13 online copy of appointment letter and and copy of bank statement at Ex.P.19.
Ex . P.13
shows that the petitioner is a Insurance Agent and Ex.P.19 shows that some amounts are credited to his Bank account but, it does not show the sourced of the account or regularity in the credits.
Therefore, these documents are not related to the petitioner's work.
Moreover, the petitioner has not examined any witness to prove his earnings.
The accident occurred in the year 2017.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.11,000/- per month.
At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 50 years as could be made out from Exs.P.15 to 17/Notarized copy of Aadhar Card, PAN Card, DL.
He was hale and healthy before the accident.

Keeping all the above SCCH - 25 12 MVC No. 6361/2018 things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:-
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:-

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Jeevika Hospital, Marathahalli and thereafter shifted to Vikram Hospital, wherein he was admitted and treated as an inpatient and was diagnosed and underwent surgery.
Considering that the nature of injury he has undergone is grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.60,000/- under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines,
conveyance, food and nourishment and other incidental expenses etc.
In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Exs.P.10 & P.22 for a sum of Rs.8,464/- and Rs.38,363/-.

Out of these bills, Ex.P.10 are not related to the injuries suffered by the petitioner since, the description is sensodyne deep clean, Navarathna Oil, milkybar, fruit and nut silk, revlon dark brown color,
Amruth Bindu for Rs.2,293/- is deducted from SCCH - 25 13 MVC No. 6361/2018 Rs.8,464/-.
And in the Ex.P.22. Bill Nos.3 & 5 are relating to Ophthalmology for Rs.14,130/- are also deducted from Rs.38,363/-.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled only for Rs.30,404/-.
There is no contrary evidence against these bills from the Respondents.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the above said amount under this head.

Ravi Shankar .K.B vs Naveen .N on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136487906/
5 iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-

entities.text: Ravi Shankar .K.B vs Naveen .N on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner has not produced discharge summary of Jeevika Hospital and Vikram Hospital to show the duration and treatment in the said hospital.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least One month time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.11,000/- under this head.

iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:-
The counsel for the respondent No.3 has argued that the petitioner has not suffered any loss of financial income since SCCH - 25 14 MVC No. 6361/2018 he is still running a factory.
During his cross examination, PW.1 has stated that he owns an interior factory in Peenya.
However, he goes on to say that he is not going to the factory.
Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the factory is closed.
Therefore, it can be assumed that the factory is still running and the petitioner has not suffered any financial Loss.
Hence, he is not entitled to any compensation under this head.
(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:-

The Petitioner was aged about 50 years at the time of accident. He has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 12%
functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.

Therefore,
considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.
SCCH - 25 15 MVC No. 6361/2018  (vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND  NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals, admitted as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:

As per the version of PW.2, the Petitioner has to undergo another surgery for removal Ravi Shankar .K.B vs Naveen .N on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136487906/
6 of implants and the estimation of this surgery is around Rs.1,50,000/-.
In this regard petitioner has produced estimation bill of Manipal Hospital stating that the estimated cost (approx) is of Rs.1,50,000/-.

As per the evidence of Pws.1 & 2 and looking at the earlier treatment cost and nature of injury and the evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.25,000/- is awarded to the Petitioner under this head.
Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.25,000/- under this head.

The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.60,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs.30,404/-
3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.11,000/- period 4. Loss of future income NIL 5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/- happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/- nourishment charges 7.

Future Medical Expenses Rs.25,000/-
TOTAL Rs.1,66,404/-
If it is rounded off it comes to around Rs.1,67,000/- and same is awarded under different heads to the Petitioner.

18. LIABILITY:
As discussed above the Respondent Nos.2 & 3 have failed to prove their defence about the accident.
Therefore, the Respondents No.2 & 3 being the RC owner and the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.25,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of SCCH - 25 17 MVC No. 6361/2018 Rs.1,67,000/-. alongwith interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.

Accordingly,
Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
19. Issue No.3:-

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-

.

Draw decree accordingly.
